# Model Overview (for Diagnosis)

The probes assume a two-layer, pre-norm BERT4Rec encoder: scaled item embeddings plus absolute position embeddings, dropout, bidirectional attention with PAD-key masking, and final normalization. Serving left-pads histories, retains at most `maxlen−1` items, and appends reserved MASK. Candidate logits use the final MASK representation through `view.predict_score`; deletion never moves the readout.

# Diagnosis Inputs & Hooks

`DiagnosisProbe(view, device)` accesses the actual network through `view.model`, plus `item_emb`, `log2feats`, `predict_score`, training histories, metadata, and dataset routing. The loader supplies `(None, sequence, positive, negative)` with matching B×L tensors.

Before sensitivity analysis, sampler checks verify reserved tokens, MASK at supervised positions, and valid distinct positive/negative IDs. Serving parity reloads the current category’s exported checkpoint, verifies exact state-tensor identity, and compares explicit encoder, ModelView, internal scoring, exported prediction, and batched outputs. Short, full-length, and truncated histories must pass score tolerances and identical ranking checks.

# Probes & Metrics

- **Embedding alignment:** Maps mean off-diagonal cosine among up to 2,048 sampled real-item embeddings into [0,1]. Larger values indicate alignment; 0.5 indicates approximately zero mean cosine, without proving representation quality.
- **Sampled-pair separation:** Across at most ten loader batches, reports mean/p10 positive-minus-negative margins, negative-win rate, and margins below 0.5. Larger margins and fewer negative wins indicate stronger in-sample separation.
- **History sensitivity:** Samples up to 64 training users and one eligible endpoint each, using a fixed target plus 99 unique prefix-excluded negatives. Reports paired score, rank, reciprocal-rank, hit@10, overlap, and ranking-agreement changes with bootstrap intervals. Sensitivity alone is neither good nor bad.

# Perturbation & Tests

History variants delete equally many recent or older items into PAD holes, preserving positions, or swap the final two items.

A nominally 30-second residual-patching pilot corrupts the latest item using frequency/recency-matched donors, then restores or disrupts residuals before either attention layer. Exploration selects sites/signs; disjoint confirmation users support sign tests. Identity, final-history structural-zero, MASK-restoration, norm-matched random, and unrelated-history controls accompany effects.
